title: Edge TLS cert rotation triggered 5xx waves and client retry spiral - mitigation and postmortem work
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Summary:
During a scheduled edge TLS certificate rotation for a small set of regions we observed a correlated spike of 5xx errors and customer escalations (n=12 customers, some on Dedicated). The surface symptom was a rapid series of connection resets and TLS negotiation failures at the frontdoor edge. Client SDKs (aggressive default retries) immediately retried, creating bursts that amplified backend KV cache thrash and connection churn, leading to additional timeouts and 5xx responses in Hosted API pools.

Impact:
- Short-lived (~8–25 minutes) but high-severity user-visible errors and increased latency for streaming calls.
- Affected customers: 12 flagged escalations, including two Dedicated customers experiencing degraded throughput.
- Observability showed token-level retry amplification and worker-side KV cache compaction activity coincident with the window.

Immediate triage notes (what we observed):
- Edge frontdoor served TLS errors with ALERT handshake failures; cert chain in a minority of frontdoor pools mismatched during rolling rotation.
- SDK clients retried (default 3x fast retries) and opened new connections rapidly instead of backing off.
- Worker processes saw increased connection churn which triggered KV cache eviction thresholds causing eviction storms and longer cold path latencies.
- Canary/burst protection rules in autoscaler were temporarily ineffective for streaming-heavy tenants.

Root cause hypothesis (converging):
1) A certificate rollout scripting bug produced a short window where a subset of edge instances served a cert bundle missing an intermediate CA, causing client TLS verification failures.
2) The SDKs' retry configuration (fast immediate backoffs) multiplied the number of concurrent connections during the window.
3) The runtime’s KV cache eviction policy, tuned for steady-state, is brittle under sudden connection surges and induced long-tail work which produced backend timeouts and 5xxs.

Short-term mitigation applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 09:42 UTC: Edge operators paused certificate rollout and restored last-known-good cert bundle to affected pools (rollback completed 09:53 UTC) — immediate reduction in TLS failures.
- 2026-03-10 09:50 UTC: Emergency hotpatch deployed to edge to accept cert chain variants (temporary tolerant mode) while root cause examined.
- 2026-03-10 10:10 UTC: SDK-side advisory published and temporary server-side gentle-reject header implemented to instruct older SDKs to apply exponential backoff (header: X-Redwood-Backoff: advised).
- 2026-03-10 10:30 UTC: Worker autoscaler threshold adjusted to add buffer capacity and KV cache compaction frequency increased to reduce long-lived eviction stalls.

Planned engineering work (this ticket):
- 1) Fix the certificate rollout orchestration to validate intermediate chains and run a dry-run verification step pre-rollout (owner: infra-sre).
- 2) Add a short-term runtime guard to detect bursty TLS negotiation failures and enable connection draining on affected pools automatically (owner: edge-team).
- 3) SDK defensive defaults: change default client retry behavior for streaming endpoints to use jittered exponential backoff and a max concurrency cap; publish patch for minor SDK versions (owner: client-sdk).
- 4) Runtime KV cache resilience: tune eviction algorithm to prioritize stable keys, and add a burst-protection mode that avoids expensive compaction during short-lived connection storms (owner: runtime-team).
- 5) Observability and alerts: add a metric series for TLS-neg-fraction, request-retry-amplification-ratio, and KV-eviction-rate; create an escalation playbook to auto-notify SRE when amplification > 2.0 (owner: observability).
- 6) Postmortem and customer comms: prepare a post-incident report, specific runbook additions, and individualized follow-up for affected customers (owner: ops/CS).

Acceptance criteria / definition of done for this ticket:
- certificate rollout script has validation step deployed and exercised in staging, and rollout pipelines updated (release: runtime-1.24).
- edge auto-drain guard in place and tested in chaos-run (no false positives).
- SDK minor releases for go/python/js published with updated retry defaults and README noted to customers migrating.
- KV cache changes deployed behind a runtime feature flag and validated with synthetic surge tests reducing 99th percentile latency by >30% in stress windows.
- Observability dashboards and alerts in place with documented oncall procedures.

Non-goals for this ticket:
- Rewriting the entire retry policy across all customer SDKs (we'll do incremental releases starting with streaming clients).
- Deep refactor of certificate management library (that is separate infra-sre project).
